brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.evidence: Three piece cells (piece at q=-1,0,1, level 0) with two jointBolts and solid caps; check_build clear.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Three hex-acc-keyhole accessories (on slot 4 of each cell). Placement is accepted, but I could not verify that slot 4 faces the wall, and no wall screws or fit were checked.
Six hex-acc-hook plates (12 hooks) on slots 1 and 2 of each cell. The hook geometry is in place, but I did not verify tool fit, and no hand tools are hung on them in the model.

requirements.requirement: Material strength and load for holding tools, and wall fixing suitability
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It does not model material, strength, or load ratings.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell horizontal tool rack: three hex base pieces in a row (q = -1, 0, 1), joined by two joint bolts, with the open faces capped. Three keyhole hangers sit on one face of each cell, and six hook plates (12 hooks) sit on two faces of each cell for small hand tools. The configurator reports meshClash clear and no rule errors. I did not confirm which face is the wall-facing one, so the keyhole orientation is unverified. Hand tools were not placed on the hooks, since the configurator only lets cable coils, gaffer tape or FPV goggles hang on hook plates.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
